quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. This makes it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slowly reduce your speed by closing the throttle, and move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It takes less time to speed up but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and to stop.
It takes more time to speed up but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase how far back you follow other vehicles.
Get closer to the vehicle in front of you.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get closer to the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and follow at a greater distance to avoid crashes. Use the lights of vehicles ahead to see the road. Use your high beam, but switch to low beam when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Means they see you.
Will never happen.
Does not guarantee they will give you the right of way.
Guarantees they will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact. Many drivers look at motorcyclists but do not actually see them or notice them.

questions.question: You should do all of the following to reduce your chance of a crash, except:

options.text: Be visible by wearing the right clothes and using your headlight.
Show your intentions by using turn signals and brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.
Hope other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible, show your intentions, and keep space around you. Look for hazards and be ready to react. Do not hope drivers see you—make sure they do.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Lean into the slippery part to stay balanced.
Keep your speed to improve grip.
Not worry about road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads when you can. If you must ride on one, keep your motorcycle straight and go slowly.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
It is hard to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load makes the motorcycle harder to balance by raising its center of gravity.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best protection if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.
It fits snugly.
It has no defects.
It has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has cracks.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must be DOT certified, fit snugly all around, and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: When riding at night, the minimum following distance should be:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds behind the vehicle ahead. You may need extra time to notice they have stopped and extra space to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: When a crash occurs, most riders are:

options.text: Riding at speeds slower than 30 mph.
Traveling for hours before the crash.
Riding at speeds faster than 75 mph.
On a trip of more than 30 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding at speeds slower than 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen when riders are going slower than 30 mph. Most crashes occur on short trips of less than five miles.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
You should sound your horn to get the driver to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Start and finish all passing moves in areas where passing is legal and safe.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means the driver sees you.
Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
Guarantees the driver will properly yield to you.
May make the driver mad.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know if a driver will yield. Drivers often look at motorcycles but do not see them.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and ease off the throttle. Brake slowly on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: You should use more space between you and other vehicles when:

options.text: Roads are slippery.
It is sunny outside.
It is colder than usual.
You are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: Use a two-second following distance normally. Increase this distance when roads are wet or icy, as these conditions increase your stopping distance.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to improve your view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to improve your view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When vehicles enter the highway from an entrance ramp on your right, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left portion of your lane so they can share the lane, if necessary.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles merging from entrance ramps. Change lanes away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, check the controls and learn the gear pattern. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.

questions.question: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden moves.
Use only the front brake.
Avoid the center of the lane on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes when needed. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, and areas that stay wet or frozen.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should riders do?

options.text: Only use mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT be:

options.text: Free of scratches.
Clear on the sides.
Airtight.
Fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, allow clear side views, fasten securely, and let air through. An airtight shield can fog up and block your vision.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Position yourself to stay out of other vehicles' blind spots, see and be seen better, avoid road hazards, avoid wind blasts, and have an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers won't try to share your lane.
